## 6. End-to-End Inter-Module Execution Lifecycle

```
==================================================================================================
[1. INITIALIZATION, GIT NETWORK DISCOVERY & CONTENT DEDUPLICATION]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
MasterFile (MF)                   GreatProcessor (gp)               TableEngine (G.TE) / DB
  │                                       │                                 │
  ├─ resolve_git_network_and_repo() ─────►│ Ingests m_project (slug = repositories[].project, §7.1.1),
  │                                       │ m_git_network (root_commit_hash, `<slug>-network`) and
  │                                       │ m_repository for target git tree; sets gp.project_slug
  ├─ ingest_git_dag(version_or_ref) ─────►│ Registers commit DAG, parents (m_commit_parent),
  │                                       │ contributors, and m_git_ref (m_v_main); gp.VID = head_cid
  │                                       │ and, for the new commits, m_commit_relation / m_commit_link
  │                                       │ (Fixes:, reverts, backports, Cc: stable, Link:; prefixes resolved
  │                                       │ with one git cat-file per range)
  │                                       │ Done version: skipped. Interrupted one: rolled back (§4.1).
  │                                       │ ingest_state.begin(): INGEST_PARSING + id watermarks
  ├─ Step 1.5: the previous version's checkpoint expanded when it is a delta (§4.2)
  ├─ Step 2: the declared ast_index / file_name_index ensured (no index duplicating a primary key)
  ├─ checkout_version(vname, base)        ├─ init_db_layout(gp)             │
  │  (Clones git tree to /dev/shm)        │  (Populates gp.Table_Array)     │
  ├─ generate_change_list(gp) ───────────►│                                 │
  │  (Populates gp.Change_List)           │                                 │
  ├─ Content Blob Hash Enumeration:       │                                 │
  │  └── git ls-tree -r {version} ───────►│ Populates gp.file_blob_hashes   │
  │                                       │                                 │
  ├─ G.TE.start(gp.Table_Array) ──────────┼────────────────────────────────►
  │  (Step 4.4, timed: preloads te_cached tables & packs 1GB/2MB/THP shared buffer)
  │                                       │                                 │
  └─ Content-Addressable Blob Dedup (Step 4.5, _reuse_parsed_blobs):       │
     └── Looks (blob_hash, ftype) up in the TableEngine m_file_blob cache; one query on m_bridge_tag
         - Reused files: m_file_name / m_bridge_checkpoint staged via the TableEngine
         - Remaining new/modified files: dispatched to multicore workers (pre-existing blobs among
           them recorded in m_ingest_blob first, §4.1)
==================================================================================================
[2. MULTICORE PARTITIONING & TWO-STAGE PARALLEL WORKER PARSING]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Main Process (trigger_multicore)          Worker Process 1..N
  │                                       │ (Inherits shared huge-page mmap across fork;
  │                                       │  calls G.TE.start_new_db(is_worker=True))
  ├─ Partition gp.worker_change_list (or gp.Change_List):
  │  ├── order_changed_files()
  │  │   └── Kahn's topological sort on header '#include' dependencies
  │  ├── Stage 1: header_files (.h, .hpp) ──►│ ChangeSet(header_diff_line)
  │  │                                       │ ├── CS.blob_hash = gp.file_blob_hashes[path]
  │  │                                       │ ├── CS.parse() -> C/ASM/Kconfig/Rust Parsers
  │  │                                       │ ├── Table.<op>() builders (m_ast.view, m_tag.set)
  │  │                                       │ ├── CS.preprocess_ref_views()
  │  │                                       │ ├── CS.prune_unchanged_dependencies()
  │  │                                       │ ├── CS.store() (Buffers into CS.cs)
  │  │                                       │ └── CS.clear_bloat()
  │  │                                       └─► Per-worker pipe: one pickled result frame per batch, then a done frame
  │  ├── processing_dirs() (Returns new directory ChangeSets, ingested while workers parse)
  │  ├── processing_unchanges() (Propagates unchanged files into m_bridge_checkpoint; returns forgotten /
  │  │   missing files, parsed by workers as an extra Stage 1 batch set before header resolution)
  │  ├── scheduler.resolve_headers() (Resolves & evacuates header ChangeSets; Stage 1 workers terminate & Clang memory is reclaimed)
  │  │
  │  ├── Stage 2: source_files (.c, .S) ───►│ Spawn Stage 2 Workers per epoch with file-scoped shared symbol segments
  │  │                                       │ ├── CS.blob_hash = gp.file_blob_hashes[path]
  │  │                                       │ ├── CS.parse() -> C/ASM/Kconfig/Rust Parsers
  │  │                                       │ ├── CS.preprocess_ref_views()
  │  │                                       │ ├── CS.pre_resolve_operations(shared_symbols) (Worker-side view unpacking & ref resolution)
  │  │                                       │ ├── CS.clear_bloat()
  │  │                                       │ └── Per-worker pipe -> reader thread (holds up to _PREFETCH_DEPTH = 8 serialized batches)
  │  │                                       └─► DependencyScheduler.ingest_batch() (Sub-millisecond lock-free staging into TableEngine)
  │  └── symlink_files
  │      (Appended to gp.Symlink_List for zero-duplication deferred alias)
  │
  └─ scheduler.finalize() (Drains deferred queue, runs Phase 2 waves, unmaps the shared symbol segments)
[3. TWO-PHASE EXECUTION: STREAMING LEAF RESOLUTION & WAVE-BASED MULTICORE STAGING]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PHASE 1: Streaming Ingestion & Opportunistic Leaf Execution (pipeline/multicore.py:trigger_multicore)
  │
  ├─ Worker Pool (G.CPUS) parses files, populating CS.foreign_deps in CS.ref()
  ├─ Streams uncompressed batches into DependencyScheduler.ingest_batch()
  ├─ Single-Compression Streaming Ingestion: Source ChangeSets execute directly on arrival, evacuating internal
  │  AST buffers before storing into gp.ChangeSet_Dict (eliminating double-compression of bloated un-evacuated ASTs).
  ├─ Event-Driven Wakeups: a ChangeSet blocked on a file of this update that is still in flight waits on it
  │  (headers wait on every in-flight file they reference before running); when that file executes, its waiters
  │  run immediately, cascading, so most files resolve while the workers are still parsing.
  │  ├─ Success: extract_tags_and_evacuate_cs(CS) & registers resolved_symbols, file_pre_extracted_tags, file_blob_ids
  │  └─ Blocked on nothing that will complete: deferred (retried at epoch boundaries, stubbed by Phase 2)
  ├─ As soon as parsing workers finish, trigger_multicore() exits immediately
  └─ Phase 1 worker pool terminates cleanly -> Clang C-heap memory purged via reclaim_system_memory()
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PHASE 2: Wave-Based Resolution & Zero-Copy Staging (pipeline/scheduler.py:execute_phase2_parallel_waves)
Main Process (In-Process Wave Resolution)       TableEngine & Database
  │                                               │
  ├─ Extracts remaining unexecuted ChangeSets     │
  ├─ Builds wave DAG:                             │
  │  deps[path] = {target in cs.foreign_deps if target in remaining}
  │                                               │
  ├─ Loop while remaining:                        │
  │  ├─ Wave Selection (ready queue, sorted):      │
  │  │  wave = files whose deps all executed; completions feed the next wave
  │  ├─ [PRECISION CYCLE BREAKING] If wave empty: │
  │  │  ├─ Selects single top candidate inside a  │
  │  │  │  source SCC (`_source_scc_candidates()`)│
  │  │  ├─ Executes with force_stubs=True and logs│
  │  │  │  unresolved ops; tracks `cycle_breaks`  │
  │  │  └─ Evacuates buffers, updates symbols,    │
  │  │     unlocking unblocked dependents in wave │
  │  │                                            │
  │  └─ [IN-PROCESS WAVE RESOLUTION]              │
  │     ├─ Iterates over wave directly in-process (zero IPC, zero pickling)
  │     ├─ cs.execute() resolves against in-memory symbols & TableEngine
  │     ├─ Still blocked although every dependency executed (e.g. a symbol the changed
  │     │  header never defines, such as a Clang implicit declaration): re-executes with
  │     │  force_stubs=True; a ChangeSet is never evacuated with unresolved operations
  │     ├─ extract_tags_and_evacuate_cs(cs) evacuates AST buffers
  │     ├─ Preserves negative query cache across micro-commits
  │     └─ G.TE.commit_all() every chunk_commit_interval (e.g. 1000 files)
  ▼
Phase 2 Wave Resolution completes at 350-700 files/s
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Main Process (STEP 6.1+: Post-Processing Subsystems) TableEngine (G.TE)          Database (G.DB)
  │                                               │                                 │
  ├─ STEP 6.1: processing_symlinks()              │                                 │
  │  ├─ norm_target = normpath(target)            │                                 │
  │  ├─ target_fid = get_fid_for_path(norm_target)│                                 │
  │  ├─ m_bridge_file.set(vid, sym_fnid, fid) ──►│ (Direct zero-duplication alias) │
  │  ├─ Broken symlink whose blob is already      │                                 │
  │  │  parsed (tagged) -> relinked to that blob  │                                 │
  │  │  (_reuse_parsed_symlink_blobs, no re-parse)│                                 │
  │  └─ Other broken symlinks -> file_processing  │                                 │
  │                                               │                                 │
  ├─ Post-Processing Subsystems:                  │                                 │
  │  ├─ processing_git_commits(version) ─────────►│ (Zero-decompression tag mapping │
  │  │                                            │  via file_pre_extracted_tags)   │
  │  ├─ processing_maintainer_files(version) ────►│                                 │
  │  ├─ processing_kbuild(version) ──────────────►│                                 │
  │  ├─ processing_arch_layouts(version) (Step 6.8: m_arch_root -> shared m_arch_layout rows, bulk insert_rows) ──►│
  │  ├─ processing_source_facts(version) (Step 6.9: m_blob_facts the database lacks, families 1-6) ──►│
  │  └─ Kernel-only steps (processing_kbuild, processing_maintainer_files, processing_arch_layouts) return
  │     at once for a project that is not a kernel tree (kernel_steps_apply(): gp.project_slug "man-pages")
  │                                               │                                 │
  ├─ Final Teardown Commit:                       │                                 │
  │  └─ G.TE.commit_all(update_in_mem_indexes=False) ──────────────────────────────►│
  │                                               │                                 │
  └─ finish_version_ingest(): INGEST_DONE, then the previous version's checkpoint becomes a delta (§4.2) ──►│
==================================================================================================
```

## 7. Configuration & SSH Port Forwarding Subsystem (`core/config.py` & `core/ssh_tunnel.py`)

### 7.1. Unified Configuration Hierarchy
- Configuration settings follow strict precedence: `CLI Flags > Environment Variables > config.json > Built-in
  Defaults`.
- When configuring or synchronizing database parameters, `DB_*` and `MYSQL_*` environment variables (including
  `DB_SOCKET`, `MYSQL_UNIX_PORT`, `MYSQL_SOCKET`) remain synchronized via `sync_environ()`, tracking
  internally exported keys in `_EXPORTED_ENV_VARS` via `_get_user_env()` to prevent environment self-pollution
  during configuration reloads. `scoped_environ(cfg)` is a context manager that exports `cfg` the same way
  for the duration of a block and then restores the previous variables and `_EXPORTED_ENV_VARS`.
- Sections:
  - `"database"`: database settings: `engine` (`"mariadb"` default, `"sqlite"`, `"mock"`; `db_engine.available_engines()`, CLI `--db`), `path` (SQLite file or `":memory:"`, exported as `DB_PATH`; a bare `database` name is not a file location and raises `ValueError` rather than creating a file in the working directory), and the MariaDB/MySQL connection settings (`host`, `port`, `user`, `password`, `database`,
    `timeout`, `unix_socket`; `user` and `password` default to empty: no account is assumed, and a
    missing credential makes the first connection fail with `db_engine.ConfigurationError` naming the keys to set), `server_tuning` (`innodb_buffer_pool_size`, `innodb_log_file_size`,
    `innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit`, `innodb_io_capacity`), and embedded feature `ssh_tunnel` (`enabled`,
    `host`, `port`, `user`, `password`, `key_file`, `remote_host`, `remote_port`, `local_port`,
    `strict_host_key_checking`, `connect_timeout`).
    - **Unix Domain Socket Support**: When `ssh_tunnel` is inactive, MariaDB connections on local hosts
      (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`) can connect via low-latency Unix domain sockets (`/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock`,
      `/var/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock`, `/tmp/mysql.sock`), bypassing the TCP loopback network stack. Controlled
      by `"unix_socket"` (`"auto"`, explicit path, or `"disabled"`/`"none"` to force TCP), environment
      variables (`DB_SOCKET` / `MYSQL_UNIX_PORT`), or CLI flag `--db-socket`.
  - `"cache"`: local cache engine (`cache_engine/CACHE_API.md`): `engine` (default `"ram"`, also `"sqlite"`, env
    `KERNELINFO_CACHE_ENGINE`) and `dir` (base directory; empty: `KERNELINFO_CACHE_DIR`, else `~/.cache/kernelinfo`).
  - `"webapp"`: FastAPI server settings (`host`, `port`, `reload`), plus `cache.max_mb` (default 1024: global
    cap of the webapp's disk cache of derived data under `KERNELINFO_CACHE_DIR`), `jobs.workers` (default 2:
    background job threads per process) `prewarm_indexes` (default `false`: build the commit relation and
    Kbuild object indexes at startup), `source_index` (`workers` default `2`, `max_mb` default `1024`,
    `revisions` default `8`: the source index's extraction processes for blobs the database lacks, their store
    cap, and how many assembled revisions stay on disk, `webapp/API.md` §2.19) and `tools`
    (`checkpatch.enabled` default `false`, `checkpatch.ref` default `"latest-release"`, `sandbox` default
    `""`: running the repository's `scripts/checkpatch.pl`, off by default); see `webapp/API.md` §2.14–§2.15,
    §2.18 and §7.1.
  - `"parser"`: TableEngine, memory mode, memory limits, `checkpoint_delta_ratio` (default
    0.3: largest share of a version's files that may differ from its base for its checkpoint to be kept as a
    delta, §4.2; 0 keeps every checkpoint full), `facts_workers` (default 4: processes of Step 6.9)
    (`table_engine`, `memory_mode`, `mem_max`: memory guard ceiling in GB, `--mm` overrides it, 0 disables the guard, `hugepages`, `preload_flush_mb`: MB of preloaded
    rows held on the heap before they are packed into a shared-memory segment, env `PRELOAD_FLUSH_MB`;
    `cache_max_table_mb`: ceiling (MB) on the size of one TE-cached table, a bigger one is read straight from
    the database instead of being cached, 0 for no ceiling, env `CACHE_MAX_TABLE_MB`, flag
    `--cache-max-table-mb`) and `symbol_layout` (`"tag"`, default: symbol rows stored once per tag; `"blob"`:
    per blob, sets `G.SYMBOL_LAYOUT`).
  - `"mailing_list"`: Mailing list ingestion feature configuration, including dedicated `ssh_tunnel` settings.
  - `"cve"`: `repo_dir` (default `"cvelistV5"`, relative to the project root): a local clone of the CVE
    Program's list (`cvelistV5`) or of the kernel CNA's `vulns.git`, ingested into `m_cve` / `m_cve_commit`
    (§9) and read from there by the webapp's CVE features (`webapp/API_ENDPOINTS.md` §4.11); not a source tree (never
    parsed as one, not under `workspace.repos_dir`).
  - `"ssh_tunnel"`: Backward compatibility alias mirroring `database.ssh_tunnel` for legacy configurations.
  - `"workspace"`: `repos_dir` (default `"repos"`, relative to the project root) holding the Git repositories
    to parse, and `auto_detect_repos` (default `true`).
  - `"repositories"`: List of tracked repositories. Each entry carries `name`, `path` (relative to the project
    root; symlinked repositories keep their `repos/<name>` path), `project`, `default_branch`, `git_url`,
    `root_commit`, `start_ref` (default: `detect_start_ref()`), `enabled`, `branch_filter` (`{"include": ["*"],
    "exclude": ["*rc*"]}`), `branches` (persisted list of active branch short names), `tag_views` (custom
    branch dropdown view entries configuring regex grouping rules for tag layouts, defaulting to
    `DEFAULT_TAG_VIEWS`), and optionally `"default": true`.
- Functions: `init_config(path)`, `get_config()`, `get_db_config()`, `get_webapp_config()`,
  `get_parser_config()`, `get_mailing_list_config()`, `get_ssh_tunnel_config(feature="database")`,
  `get_workspace_config()`, `sync_environ(cfg)`, `scoped_environ(cfg)`, `resolve_unix_socket(socket_path, host)`,
  `matches_branch_filter(branch, branch_filter)`, `find_repository_branches(repo, branch_filter,
  default_branch)`, `update_repository_branches(name_or_path, write=True)`, `project_display_name(slug)`,
  `is_kernel_project(slug)`, `repository_project(entry)`, `is_manpages_repository(name, git_url, root_commit)`.
  Constants: `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, `DEFAULT_BRANCH_FILTER`, `DEFAULT_TAG_VIEWS`, `REPOSITORY_KEYS`, `LINUX_PROJECT`,
  `MANPAGES_PROJECT`, `PROJECT_DISPLAY_NAMES`, `NON_KERNEL_PROJECTS`, `MANPAGES_ROOT_COMMIT`,
  `MANPAGES_BRANCH_FILTER`, `MANPAGES_TAG_VIEWS`.

### 7.1.1. Repository Auto-Detection & Selection
- `find_repository_dirs()` lists Git repositories (work trees, gitfiles, or bare repositories) directly under
  `workspace.repos_dir`; `detect_repository(path)` describes one (`git symbolic-ref` for the branch, falling
  back to `origin/HEAD`, then `main`/`master`; `remote.origin.url`; `rev-list --max-parents=0 --first-parent
  <branch>` for `root_commit`; `find_repository_branches()` for `branches` matching `branch_filter`). Results
  are cached per path for the process. `project` is the directory name, except for a clone rooted at
  `LINUX_ROOT_COMMIT` (`1da177e4c3f4…`, project `linux` whatever its directory name) and the Linux man-pages.
- **Linux man-pages** (`is_manpages_repository()`): a clone whose root commit is `MANPAGES_ROOT_COMMIT`
  (`fea681dafb1363a154b7fc6d59baa83d2a9ebc5c`), whose directory is `man-pages`, or whose `origin` URL ends in
  `/man-pages.git` (or `/man-pages`) is detected as project `man-pages`: `default_branch` `master` when no
  branch is checked out, `start_ref` = `root_commit` (tagged `man-pages-1.70`), `branch_filter`
  `MANPAGES_BRANCH_FILTER` (`master` only), and `tag_views` `MANPAGES_TAG_VIEWS` (one view grouping
  `^(man-pages-\d+)(\..*)$` by major release). Other repositories are detected as described above.
  `config.example.json` lists both the `linux` and the `man-pages` entries.
- **Projects** (`m_project`): `main.resolve_git_network_and_repo()` registers each repository under the slug of
  its entry's `project` (`main.repo_project_slug()`: else `man-pages` for a tree rooted at
  `MANPAGES_ROOT_COMMIT`, else `linux`), named by `project_display_name()` ("Linux Kernel" for `linux`,
  "Linux man-pages" for `man-pages`, otherwise the slug); a new network is named `<slug>-network`, and a tree
  whose root commit already has a network reuses it. Projects in `NON_KERNEL_PROJECTS` (`man-pages`) are
  parsed like any tree (their pages are `T_RAW` files) but skip the kernel-only work: Kbuild rules, MAINTAINERS
  matching and ARCH layouts per version (§6), the CVE list ingestion and its commit resolution at start (§9),
  the automatic Kbuild backfill (§12). The tag-driven steps run for every project: release statistics (§10)
  and the master role's delegation of stable / `next` chains (§11), both from the repository's own release
  tags (`parser/git_ast/release_order.release_tag_names()`).
- `detect_start_ref(repo, root_commit, branches)` picks the first version to parse: among the first-parent
  roots of the default branch and of every `history/*` branch, the root whose release tag sorts first,
  named by that tag (Linux with the bootlin `linux-history` remote: `0.01`, root of
  `history/0.10-fix-RCS`, before `2.4.0` of `history/master` and `v2.6.12-rc2` of `master`). A tag name
  makes `get_version_tags()` walk every later release tag, across the unconnected history roots. Without
  history roots (or tags on them) it is `root_commit`.
- `sync_repositories(write=True)` adds newly found repositories and fills keys missing from known entries
  without overwriting user-set values, then atomically rewrites the loaded config file (`config.json`),
  preserving all other keys. `main.py` runs it on every start when `auto_detect_repos` is true; `python3
  main.py --detect-repos` runs it, prints the repositories with branch counts, and exits.
- `update_repository_branches(name_or_path=None, write=True)` refreshes the discovered `branches` list for the
  matching repository and atomically persists it to `config.json`, ordering discovered branches in deterministic
  topological and chronological tiers: `history/*` (Tier 0: `history/master`, Tier 1: secondary history branches) $\to$
  Tier 2: mainline trunk (`master` / `main`) $\to$ Tier 3: `stable/*` series (version-ordered: `linux-2.6.11.y` $\to$
  `linux-7.3.y`) $\to$ Tier 4: `linux-next/*` integration branches (`linux-next/master` first, then topic branches) $\to$
  Tier 5: remaining topic branches.
- `get_repositories_config()` returns enabled repositories, merging undetected-but-present ones in memory (no
  write). `get_repository(name_or_path=None)` looks a repository up by name or path, or returns the default
  (`"default": true`, else the first). `get_default_repo_path()` / `resolve_repo_path(entry)` return absolute
  paths; the webapp's `LINUX_REPO_DIR` is `get_default_repo_path()`.
- **Commit DAG**: `ingest_git_dag()` ingests the complete history of the first version (no implicit
  1,000-commit cap) and every commit of later ranges, merges included (see `parser/git_ast/GIT_API.md` §6);
  `--limit N` bounds the commits recorded per range. Shared commit history across branches is
  content-deduplicated per `network_id` in `m_commit` and `m_file_blob`.
- **Default parse target**: Without `--ref`, `main()` starts at the selected repository's `start_ref` (its
  first version by default, `detect_start_ref()`) and continues through every subsequent release tag (`get_version_tags`).
  `--branches` (or `--all-branches`) automatically refreshes `config.json` and ingests the tip commit of every
  branch matching `branch_filter` as an independent checkpoint (`m_git_ref` with `ref_type = 2`). `--repo`
  accepts a configured repository name or a filesystem path.
- **TUI Management**: `RepositoriesScreen` and `RepoDetailScreen` (`core/tui/screens/repos.py`) provide interactive
  curses management of configured git repositories, `workspace.repos_dir` scanning, default branches, start refs,
  branch filtering rules, tag grouping regex presets (`DEFAULT_TAG_VIEWS`), and diagnostic validation via `test_repository()`.
  In `RepoDetailScreen`, `↑`/`↓` move between rows inside the Branches and Tag View Regex Rules boxes and leave a box only
  past its first/last row (`Tab`/`Shift-Tab` always switch widgets); `Space` toggles the highlighted branch, and on the rules
  box `Enter` edits, `A`/`Insert` adds (after the highlighted rule, same tag view), and `D`/`Delete` removes the highlighted
  regex rule. Rules are validated with `re.compile` before they are applied; a tag view left without rules is dropped.

### 7.2. SSH Tunnel Manager (`SSHTunnelManager`)
- **Purpose**: Encrypts and forwards remote connections across hosts (e.g. MariaDB database or mailing list
  services), allowing local orchestration workers to reach remote instances securely without exposing ports
  over public networks. Disabled by default (`enabled: false`).
- **Per-Feature Architecture**:
  - Tunnels are configured per feature (embedded within each feature's configuration section such as
    `database.ssh_tunnel` and `mailing_list.ssh_tunnel`).
  - Multiple feature tunnels can run concurrently without collision, each binding to its own configured or
    dynamically assigned local ephemeral port.
  - Backward compatibility: Legacy flat `ssh_tunnel` definitions in configuration files automatically migrate
    into `database.ssh_tunnel`.
- **Subprocess Execution**: Uses system OpenSSH binary (`/usr/bin/ssh`) via `subprocess.Popen` with `-N -L
  <local_port>:<remote_host>:<remote_port>`, `-o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes`, `-o ServerAliveInterval=15`, `-o
  ServerAliveCountMax=3`. `detach_tty=True` starts the process in a new session (`start_new_session`), so it
  has no controlling terminal to prompt on.
- **Dynamic Port Binding**: If `local_port` is 0 or already occupied, dynamically allocates an ephemeral
  localhost port to avoid collisions with any local services.
- **Authentication**:
  - Private key: Configurable path via `key_file` (`-i <key> -o IdentitiesOnly=yes`).
  - Password: Supports non-interactive authentication via `sshpass` (if installed) or dynamically provisioned
    secure `SSH_ASKPASS` helper scripts (with `SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force`).
  - User: Custom login username via `-l <user>` / `user@host`.
  - Host Key Verification: Defaults to `accept-new`, configurable to `no` or `yes`.
- **Lifecycle Integration**:
  - Invoked during startup via `start_ssh_tunnel(cfg=None, feature="database")`.
  - Probes local port socket connectivity until listening (up to `connect_timeout` seconds) before declaring
    readiness.
  - Automatically updates active configuration: for `"database"`, sets `db_cfg["host"] = "127.0.0.1"`,
    `db_cfg["port"] = local_port` and calls `sync_environ()`, transparently routing `G.DB` and all
    multiprocessing workers through the tunnel. For other features (e.g. `"mailing_list"`), updates the
    feature's active host and port settings.
  - Individual teardown via `stop_ssh_tunnel(feature)` or comprehensive teardown via `stop_ssh_tunnel()`
    (registered with `atexit` and `G.emergency_shutdown()`).
- **One Tunnel Per Run (Fork Ownership)**: Both tunnels are opened once before any version is parsed -
  `database.ssh_tunnel` in `arg_handling()`, and `mailing_list.ssh_tunnel` in `main()` (when both
  `mailing_list.enabled` and `mailing_list.ssh_tunnel.enabled` are set), so no tunnel is opened by the `-u` /
  `-T` test paths, which never reach `main()`. Every forked per-version worker reuses that single forward
  instead of opening its own:
  - A tunnel is **owned** by the process that spawned its `ssh` child (`_owner_pid`, `is_owner()`). A fork
    inherits the manager object, and the forward itself is just a TCP listener on `127.0.0.1`, usable from any
    process.
  - `is_active()` in a non-owner process must not call `Popen.poll()`: `waitpid()` on a process that is not
    our child fails with `ECHILD`, which CPython reports as a clean exit (`returncode = 0`), so a worker would
    conclude the tunnel is dead and open a second one. The inherited forward is validated instead by
    `_pid_alive(proc.pid) and _is_port_in_use(local_port)`.
  - `stop()` in a non-owner process only drops the local handle. Signalling the inherited `ssh` PID would tear
    down the parent's tunnel for every other worker, and the askpass script belongs to the owner. This also
    makes `stop_ssh_tunnel()` safe to call unconditionally in a worker (see `_git_commit_worker`'s
    `client.close(stop_tunnel=True)`), which reaps a tunnel a worker did have to open itself rather than
    orphaning the `ssh` process when the worker exits.

### 7.3. Interactive Terminal User Interface (TUI) Configuration Subsystem (`core/tui/`)
- **Zero-Dependency Architecture**: Built entirely on Python standard library `curses` without external UI packages.
- **Triggering & CLI Invocation**:
  - Explicit CLI arguments: `python3 main.py --configure` or `--config-tui` launches the TUI directly.
  - Automatic fallback: If no configuration file is detected (`find_config_path() is None`) and standard input is an interactive terminal (`sys.stdin.isatty() is True`), `main.py` launches `run_config_tui()` automatically. Non-interactive environments (CI/cron/pipelines) fall back to built-in defaults without prompting.
  - **Pipeline launch hand-off**: `pipeline/cli.py` (`arg_handling()`) calls `run_config_tui_launch()`, which returns `None` when the user exits and otherwise a dict of CLI argument overrides that `arg_handling()` sets on the argparse namespace (`setattr(args, key, value)`) before `init_config()` reads the configuration file (`{}` for a plain run). When `setup_memory_limit()` re-execs under `systemd-run`, `KERNELINFO_TUI_LAUNCH` carries the JSON-encoded overrides across `execvp` so the child process applies them and skips re-opening `--configure`. `run_config_tui()` returns `run_config_tui_launch() is not None`. Screens request a launch with `TUIApp.request_launch(save=False, **launch_args)`, which saves first only with `save=True`, stores `TUIApp.launch_args`, and exits the event loop; a failed save leaves the TUI running. `TUIApp.disk_config()` returns the configuration as saved on disk. `core/tui/screens/launch.py` holds the shared flow: `choose_launch_config(stdscr, app, action)` returns `RUN_SAVED` without unsaved edits and otherwise asks `Save & <action>` (`SAVE_AND_RUN`) / `Use saved config.json` (`RUN_SAVED`) / `Cancel` (`None`); `launch_pipeline(stdscr, app, mode, **launch_args)` calls `request_launch()` and reports a failed save.
  - `reset_only` launch override: after the table reset in `main()` (`args.reset`), `args.reset_only` exits through `G.emergency_shutdown(0)` without parsing.
- **Screen Navigation & Lifecycle (`core/tui/app.py`, `core/tui/screens/`)**:
  - `TUIApp`: Orchestrates the curses lifecycle (`curses.wrapper`), manages a screen stack (`push_screen`, `pop_screen`, `current_screen`), tracks configuration dirty state (`is_dirty`), and performs atomic JSON persistence via temporary file replacement. Loading moves a legacy top-level `ssh_tunnel` section into `database.ssh_tunnel` when the latter is absent (as `load_config()` does), and `save_config()` writes `database.ssh_tunnel` as the only database tunnel section (the top-level alias is left out of the file).
  - `ModalDialog.show()` resolves to the highlighted button when `getch()` reports no input (`-1`), so a dialog on a non-blocking window never spins.
  - **Terminal output capture (`core/tui/output_capture.py`)**: `TUIApp.run()` runs its event loop inside `TerminalOutputCapture`, which detaches log handlers that write to stdout/stderr (file handlers keep logging), collects every record through one root capture handler (also installed as `logging.lastResort`), swaps `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` for buffers, and redirects file descriptor 2 to a temporary file (child processes such as `ssh` included). Whenever captured output grows, the loop calls `clearok(True)` so the next refresh repaints every cell. After `curses.wrapper` returns, `run_config_tui()` replays the captured records and text on the restored terminal.
  - **Terminal state restore (`core/tui/app.py` `TerminalState`)**: `run_config_tui_launch()` saves the tty attributes and the dispositions of `SIGTSTP`, `SIGCONT`, `SIGWINCH`, `SIGINT`, `SIGTERM`, `SIGHUP` and `SIGQUIT` before `curses.wrapper` starts, and restores both as soon as it returns (normally or with an error), before the captured output is replayed. ncurses' `initscr()` installs C-level handlers for these signals that `endwin()` leaves in place; restoring the dispositions keeps a later `SIGTSTP`/`SIGCONT` (Ctrl+Z, `fg`) from switching the pipeline's terminal back to curses program mode (`ONLCR` off).
  - **View state**: `TUIApp.view_state` maps a screen key to its UI state (highlighted rows, focused list). `BaseScreen.remember_view(key, **state)` / `recall_view(key)` store and read it, so a screen re-created from the main menu reopens on the same rows.
  - `MainMenuScreen`: Top-level menu with hotkeys `[1-9, S, R, P, Q]` (`HOTKEYS`, case-insensitive; `Esc` = `Q`): the configuration screens (`1`-`4`), `Run Diagnostics` (`5`), `Git Repository Manager` (`6`, opens `GitRepoSelectScreen`), `Parse Specific Versions / Tags` (`7`), `Table Reset` (`8`), `DB Content Viewer` (`9`), `Save Configuration` (`S`, described as "Saves to Active Config File": writes `app.config_path`, the Active File shown in the header), `Save & Run Pipeline` (`R`, `request_launch(save=True)`), `Run Pipeline (saved config.json)` (`P`, `request_launch()` without saving; with unsaved edits it first confirms that they are discarded), and `Exit` (`Q`). Items take two rows when the list fits the menu box and one row otherwise; the list scrolls to keep the selection visible, with `↑`/`↓` markers on the box border.
  - `GitRepoSelectScreen` (`core/tui/screens/git_select.py`): repository hub in front of `GitManagerScreen`. It lists `repository_candidates()` (`core/tui/screens/git_manager.py`): the configured `repositories[]` entries that are git repositories, then the clone targets `<workspace.repos_dir>/linux` (kind `linux`) and `<workspace.repos_dir>/man-pages` (kind `man-pages`, shown as `man`) and the CVE catalog `cve.repo_dir` (kind `cve`; relative to the project root, empty means `cvelistV5`) unless a configured entry already has that path; each row shows name, kind, clone state (remote count or "not cloned") and path. The list shows the repository's remotes (name and fetch URL). Keys: `c` clones the current `linux`, `man-pages` or `cve` candidate when its directory is missing (`clone_current()`). A carriage return makes the next text replace the current line, so git progress counters update in place. `Esc`/`c` asks `Keep Running` / `Stop`; `Stop` terminates (then kills after 5 s).
